checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: Both halves are answered on the page. Medicine: ch 18 delivers the nine sound packets plus the hunter's twist as eighteen courses at Ranu. Ch 20 breaks Kiran's fever. Ch 24 brings the buyer's sack, which finishes the twenty-three untreated. Arrest: ch 32, before the meltwater runs, Rohan tells Gopal and the cairn crowd 'I am not arresting her. I am walking to Taravan beside her, with the law in her hand.' One thing stays open beside the hinge: the assembly's 'Held pending the queen's judgement' (ch 30) and Gopal's 'The queen may say otherwise' (ch 32). This reads as a legal tail, not the book's question, but the owner may want it softened so only the Old Bargain stays open.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: Every outline clue pays off or is a series thread. The four confirmation payoffs land on the page: C01, C04, C05, C07, C09, C13 and C15 in ch 16; C10 in ch 25; C21 and C22 in ch 28 and ch 30; C20 in ch 30. C25 is weakened. The planted kid bell is buried with Sunni in ch 19. Ch 32 hangs 'Badami's big bell' instead, an object never planted. The callback still names the small bell's fate, so it counts, but the substitution is visible.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: Ch 16 (midpoint). Meera confesses 'I am the Salt Fox.' Rohan answers with his writ to deliver her. Together they deduce that Varun set the avalanche and is her middleman, so 'My lifeline was your enemy's purse' and 'I trusted the man who killed Jassi.' This recasts the first half and leads directly to the first kiss and the binding promise, 'I will not let you fall on this mountain.' Enemies become complicit lovers.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: Ch 1 belief in action: she hides the count against her ribs and refuses the captain even her name ('I'd keep it. It's the one you can prove', ch 2). Ch 30 choice, before the assembly: 'My name is Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox... That is a hanging, by your law. I put it in the crown's record, under my own name, so that no one needs to guess.' She names the change aloud: 'It's a rope. It depends who ties it.' Ch 31 reinforces it when she chooses the Closing Roll for life: 'I'll owe them winters. I'd give them anyway.'

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: Ch 3: Jassi dies in the avalanche and is mourned at the waystone in ch 4 and ch 31. Ch 18: Sunni, seven, dies before dawn and is buried in ch 19. Ch 26 and ch 31: Meera's left ring and little fingers die from the great lie and are amputated by Nimmi. None of these losses is undone.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Rohan must carry the queen's lapis seal to the Snow Fair within twenty days and press it to revoke Pritam's investiture (ch 2, ch 11, ch 30). From ch 21 he also has to rescue his sister Ila, held at Garh Neshar. Both goals predate and are independent of Meera.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: Ch 32. The stones speak through every palm: 'The bargain is owed... When the fourth winter ends, the pass closes. Forever. Unless someone pays.' It is tied to the unequal carved hands, the grandfather's folded gloves, and 'the queen will want' Ila's map. It opens the next book's question without leaving the romance or the seal plot unresolved.

series_threads.thread: Two hands on one rope, 'brothers in arms' versus warden and smuggler. Ch 32 notices the hands are unequal (broad and long), so the chronicle lied. This leads into the Old Bargain.
Asha's three-nested-loop knot matches the cairn carving. Ch 28: Asha silences Meera's question about it ('Not here'). Asha's link to the old crossing is withheld.
Rohan's grandfather died on the pass the winter before the Closing Law. Ch 27 and ch 32 add the neatly folded gloves, which suggest a payment toward the Old Bargain.
The masked buyer's cut-corner Neshar silver. The buyer's identity and his access to the regent's stores are unrevealed.
The grey-bearded officer lowers the torches (ch 27) and lays his sword down at the Fair (ch 30). His name is never given.
The seal wax is mixed with the queen's own blood. This suggests blood-binding magic tied to the crown and the Bargain.
The regent's general is officially exiled, but Ranu insists otherwise. Nimmi links this to the officer on the grey horse (C18).

summary: The book meets all seven structural promises. The central question is resolved: the medicine reaches Ranu (ch 18, 20, 24) and Rohan publicly refuses to arrest Meera at the thaw (ch 32). The ch 16 midpoint reverses both the mystery (Varun) and the romance (confession, then kiss and promise). Meera's belief change is proved by a shown choice in ch 30, when she enters her own name in the crown's record, and repeated in ch 31 when she accepts the Closing Roll. Jassi, Sunni and two of Meera's fingers are lost permanently. Rohan's seal mission and his rescue of Ila are independent of her. Ch 32 opens the Old Bargain as a clean series hinge. All 26 outline clues either pay off or are logged above as series threads. The owner may want to review three items. First, C25 swaps the planted kid bell, buried with Sunni, for an unplanted 'big bell' at the cairn. Planting Meera collecting it at Kothi, or keeping the small bell, would tighten the callback. Second, Meera's status 'held pending the queen's judgement' stays open alongside the hinge. It is acceptable, but it risks reading as a second unanswered question. Third, two unlisted loose ends remain: why the queen wanted the Salt Fox 'delivered and not hanged' (ch 2), and Varun mentioning he crossed in a jogini binding. These could be logged as series threads or answered. There is also minor day-count drift in chapters 13 to 21 (nine, eight, six and five days to the Fair), which a continuity pass should reconcile.
